summary: A senator's husband handled preschool, karate and a newborn at home while she was at the capital, and said it was not easy.
realLife: A California senator's husband handled child care in Los Angeles while the Legislature met in Sacramento, driving a son to preschool and karate and caring for a newborn. An assemblyman drove two hours home to San Jose nightly during session and said the cost to a spouse and family could be painful. The article notes most lawmakers now keep their families in the district because spouses have careers.
gates: A seat is held at a capital away from home.
The household has a young child and the spouse is the home parent.
inGame: A legislature sitting away from home, a household with a young child and a spouse as the home parent can carry it.

turns.what: The official commutes home every night and sees the children daily.
turns.writesBack: Fewer nights at the capital; tired days at work.

turns.what: The spouse manages and says little.
The spouse tells the official, after the session, that it was too much.
turns.writesBack: A home talk; the official weighs not running again.
